angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 487,477 km at 42.42 pc = 0.15 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 23.5715 +/- 0.0145 mas (same row, RUWE 0.88): 42.42 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.7007 +/- 0.0575 solar radii from Mistry et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-139 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166....9M/abstract): 487,477 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.69 +/- 0.0852 solar masses from Mistry et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-139 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166....9M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4570 +/- 50 K from Mistry et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-139 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166....9M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Mistry et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-139 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166....9M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-139.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.586, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
